report.source_text: Bone marrow aspirate showed plasma cells accounting for approximately 15% (including immature plasma cells account for 5%) of total marrow cellularity, with cytoplasmic granular inclusions and needle-shaped crystals (Figure 1). Flow cytometry analysis performed on a bone marrow aspirate sample identified a monotypic, cytoplasmic kappa light chain-restricted CD38+, CD138+ plasma cell population. Cytogenetic analysis revealed 46, XX. IGH/CCND1 translocation was confirmed by fluorescence in situ hybridization analysis, while IGH/MAF and IGH/FGFR3 translocations were not found.

report.source_text: Renal biopsy revealed a total of 31 glomeruli, of which nine were globally sclerosed. Proximal tubular lesions were seen with focal atrophy and brush border disappearance. Eosinophilic needle-shaped crystals in the cytoplasm of the proximal tubular epithelial cells and podocytes were also observed. The same crystals were also noted in tubular cells shedded into tubular lumens and in some interstitial histiocytes and mesangial cells (Figure 2).

clinician.final_diagnosis: MM with CSH involving both the bone marrow and kidney, with complications of LCPT and LCCP
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old woman presented with 6 months of intermittent lower back and leg pain, nausea, vomiting, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and severe renal impairment. Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation revealed an IgG kappa monoclonal gammopathy. Bone marrow biopsy showed 15% plasma cells with cytoplasmic needle-shaped crystals, confirming plasma cell neoplasm. Kidney biopsy demonstrated tubular and glomerular lesions with eosinophilic needle-shaped crystals in proximal tubular cells, podocytes, interstitial histiocytes, and mesangial cells, consistent with crystalline deposits. She received induction chemotherapy with dexamethasone and bortezomib resulting in improved renal function.
